d: Marcy and Jefferson announce that they are expecting a baby, sending Al into pearls of laughter saying that it's the end of Jefferson's life, until Peggy announces the same.
Peggy and Marcy's constant demands for belly rubbing and expensive baby accessories drive Al crazy, prompting him to make a run for it.
When Al unearths his father's old hammer, he decides to turn the garage into his own private room to escape his pregnant wife.
Kelly earns a quick $1,000 at hustling pool to buy a gown for the local Miss Cheese competition, and a suspicious Al is out for blood, mistakenly thinking that Kelly is into prostitution.

st: Looking for a Desk in All the Wrong Places
d: While Peggy is away helping Marcy recover her precious childhood belongings that Jefferson auctioned off and gambled away the money, Al, Kelly, and Bud hold an anti-baby meeting and make plans for a new "Bundy World Order.”
While Jefferson suffers through a sympathetic pregnancy, Peggy is upset that Al is immune. Even worse Buck is listless and getting all the attention due Peggy.

st: If I Could See Me Now
d: Al keeps barely avoiding minor accidents, so Bud and Kelly try to convince him to get glasses, but he keeps insisting that his vision is perfect.
After Al falls out of his bedroom window and passes out, he claims he saw God's shoes. He decides to make and sell these shoes in order to make it big.

Al finally gets cable TV installed in the Bundy household, but he cannot find anything good to watch. All that changes when Kelly gets her own talk show “Vital Social Issues N’Stuff with Kelly” on public access TV with just $35 from her girlfriends
Al, Kelly, and Bud travel to Hollywood after Kelly's talk show becomes a hit with the TV networks.
Al dreams he's a detective on the verge of a big case.

st: So This is How Sinatra Felt
d: Peggy sends Bud and Kelly to spy on Al at the shoe store for the day to confirm her suspicion that Al's recent giddiness is the work of an extramarital affair.
Al tries to retrieve his game ball from a former girlfriend after he takes stock of his life and finds he has nothing.

As Grandmaster B, Bud does his coolest best while all over a girl who takes him out to non-traditional Bundy things such as rafting and sky diving. Meanwhile, Al and Peggy invite Marcy and Jefferson over to play a new board game called "Ethical Dilemma."
Al is asked to appear in an athletic shoe commercial. Al, being Polk High's 1966 all-city running back and shoe salesman, is glad to reclaim his glory days
